questions.question_text: In Utah, managing rental property for others for compensation requires:
distractors: Only a business license
No license for fewer than 5 units
A property management certificate only
questions.explanation: 61-2f-201(1)(d) makes it unlawful to engage in property management without a license. Exemptions exist for an owner or lessor, a salaried employee managing only that employer's property, a resident manager paid in reduced rent, a common interest association's salaried employee, and brokerage support staff (61-2f-202(1)(a), 61-2f-202.5).

questions.question_text: Utah's separate Property Manager License, created by H.B. 337 (2025), now takes effect on:
distractors: July 1, 2026
January 1, 2026
questions.explanation: H.B. 337 (2025) created the license effective January 1, 2026; H.B. 1002 in the 2025 First Special Session pushed it to July 1, 2026; and H.B. 377 (2026) extended implementation again to January 1, 2027. Until then property management is performed under a principal broker, associate broker, or sales agent license.

questions.question_text: What will the Property Manager License require of a new applicant?
questions.correct_answer: At least 24 hours of division-created training and a licensing exam
distractors: 120 hours of prelicensing education
A four-year degree in property management
A background check and nothing more
questions.explanation: 61-2f-203(1)(d)(iv) directs the Division to create a property manager education program of at least 24 hours, choosing the subjects and the proportion of hours, and 61-2f-203(1)(e) requires an examination. An active principal broker, associate broker, or sales agent may obtain the property manager license without either.

questions.question_text: A property manager in Utah must be affiliated with:
distractors: The Division of Real Estate directly
The county housing authority
The property owner's attorney
questions.explanation: Property management is performed under the brokerage, and 61-2f-302(1) requires anyone who is not a principal broker to affiliate with one. Once the property manager license takes effect, a licensed property manager engaged by or for a brokerage must also affiliate with the principal broker (61-2f-302(6)).

questions.question_text: Which duties does a licensed property manager typically perform?
questions.correct_answer: Tenant screening, rent collection, and maintenance
distractors: Property appraisal and market analysis
Title searches and insurance issuance
Loan origination and underwriting
questions.explanation: 61-2f-102(30) defines property management as securing rentals, collecting and accounting for rent, and authorizing repair expenditures. It excludes hotel and motel management, tourist rentals of under 30 consecutive days, and mineral or oil and gas leasing.

questions.question_text: A property manager collects first month's rent and a security deposit from a new tenant. These funds are:
questions.correct_answer: Trust funds requiring deposit into the PB's trust account
distractors: The property manager's earned compensation
The property owner's funds to forward immediately
Personal funds until the lease is fully executed
questions.explanation: Rent, security deposits, and other tenant money are trust funds and must reach the trust account within three business days of receipt (R162-2f-401c(1)(h)(ii)). A broker regularly managing seven or more units must keep a property management trust account separate from the real estate trust account (R162-2f-403b(1)(a)(i)).

questions.question_text: A property manager deposits tenant security deposits into their personal bank account. This is:
distractors: Acceptable for deposits under $1,000
Permitted if the PB gives verbal approval
Standard practice for small property managers
questions.explanation: Security deposits are trust funds. Putting them in a personal account is commingling and diversion under 61-2f-401(4), and the account must be a Utah bank or credit union account maintained by the principal broker (R162-2f-403b).

questions.question_text: Proper accounting for property management trust funds requires:
questions.correct_answer: Detailed records of all deposits and disbursements
distractors: Monthly summaries to the Division only
Annual reports to the property owner only
Records only when requested by the tenant
questions.explanation: R162-2f-403b requires date-sequential deposit and disbursement records with a running balance, a monthly reconciliation against both bank and client records, and Division access on request. The Division must be notified within 30 days if the account is out of balance and the imbalance cannot be cured.

questions.question_text: Who is ultimately responsible for ensuring a property management trust account is properly maintained?
distractors: The individual property manager
The property owner
The Division of Real Estate
questions.explanation: R162-2f-401c(1)(i)(ii) makes the principal broker personally responsible for deposits held in the trust account, and R162-2f-401j(2) requires the broker to train staff performing property management tasks.

questions.question_text: A property manager uses collected rent to pay for a property repair before depositing the remaining balance. This is:
questions.correct_answer: Improper; all funds must be deposited first
distractors: Acceptable if the repair was authorized
Permitted for repairs under $500
Standard practice for emergency repairs
questions.explanation: Trust funds must be deposited before any disbursement; paying an expense out of collected rent before deposit defeats the accounting rules in R162-2f-403b. Disbursements may then be made only as the management contract, lease, written authorization, or a court order allows.

questions.question_text: A property management agreement must be signed by which parties?
questions.correct_answer: The property owner and the principal broker
distractors: The property manager and the tenant
The property owner and the Division
The sales agent and the property owner
questions.explanation: R162-2f-401a(2)(d) requires a written agency agreement with the owner of a property the licensee will manage, and the agreement runs to the principal broker rather than to an individual agent.

questions.question_text: Which task may an unlicensed employee of a Utah property management company perform under the principal broker's supervision?
questions.correct_answer: Giving a prospective tenant access to a rental unit
distractors: Negotiating lease terms with a prospective tenant
Signing a property management agreement for the brokerage
Setting the rent for a managed property
questions.explanation: R162-2f-401j(3) lets unlicensed staff provide unit access, do bookkeeping and rent collection, quote rents the principal broker has set, complete pre-printed leases except for negotiated terms, serve or receive legal notices, handle complaints, and inspect units. Negotiating terms and setting rent are not on that list.

questions.question_text: A property owner gives verbal instructions to manage their rental but refuses to sign a written agreement. The broker should:
questions.correct_answer: Insist on a written agreement before managing
distractors: Proceed based on the verbal agreement
Start managing and get the signature later
Have the sales agent sign on the owner's behalf
questions.explanation: R162-2f-401a(2)(d) requires the written agreement before management services begin, and managing on a handshake leaves the broker without the agreement the rule requires.

questions.question_text: A property management agreement should include termination provisions because:
questions.correct_answer: Both parties need clear exit procedures
distractors: The Division requires 90-day notice periods
Agreements automatically expire after 1 year
Termination clauses are tax-deductible
questions.explanation: Termination provisions matter in Utah for a concrete reason: R162-2f-401j(4) requires the principal broker to deliver any trust money to the owner within 30 days of the termination of a property management contract.

questions.question_text: The authority granted to a property manager in the management agreement determines:
questions.correct_answer: What decisions the manager can make independently
distractors: The manager's license type and level
The maximum rent that can be charged
Whether the property qualifies for tax exemptions
questions.explanation: The agreement fixes the scope of the manager's authority — spending limits for repairs, lease terms that may be approved, and what needs the owner's sign-off — and R162-2f-401a(20) requires prior written authorization identifying the specific actions a licensee may take on the owner's behalf.
